_comment: Buy-side origination: home services companies with >= $500K EBITDA.
Nobody publishes EBITDA for private companies this size, so headcount is
the proxy. At home-services margins of 10-15%, $500K EBITDA implies
roughly $3.5-5M of revenue, which is about 20-30 employees. min_employees
is 20 and reads BBB's OWN headcount from the profile page -- not Apollo's
-- so a company Apollo has never indexed can still qualify. That is the
point of scraping BBB rather than querying Apollo.
A row with apollo_match = not-in-apollo AND real headcount is a company
the Apollo-first tools cannot see. Those are the sleepers; sort by that
No revenue ceiling -- the PE platform partners buy at many sizes.
MSP/IT is absent despite 5 partners wanting it: MSPs sell B2B and rarely
register with BBB, so those lists would be noise. That vertical needs an
metros: national, largest first, since deal flow follows population. The
cursor advances every run and is remembered in .rotation-state.json.
